items.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] It sounds like he learned it from Basie. [INTERVIEWEE] Maybe, yeah.

ctx.x: band, because the band would kind of work him into it. But he was pretty strong on tempos. His tempo, Sinatra, you know he liked the two-four beat. When he would do that he would finally get the band because that wasn’t where Nelson would put it. You would see a night and day between the time we’d rehearse it with Nelson and then by the time Frank started singing it, he would start popping his finger, and he could do the drummer — Irv Cottler or somebody like that, and they’d have the beat going. So it would have…
It sounds like he learned it from Basie.
